uncited: **Inputs:** Polygonal mesh (triangles), volume bounds $[x_{min}, x_{max}] \times [y_{min}, y_{max}] \times [z_{min}, z_{max}]$, volume resolution `voxelDim`, and bit-depth per voxel.
**Outputs:** A 3D voxel grid (stored as 2D texture worksheets) representing the surface or solid volume.
**Position Map:** A 2D texture (`positionMap`) where each texel stores the world-space position of the nearest surface fragment.
**Position Map Generation:** Rasterize the geometry into the `positionMap` 2D texture.
Each fragment writes its world-space position to the corresponding texel.
This step relies on the parent method's principles [Position Map and Image-Space Transfer](6237-position-map-and-image-space-transfer.md).
For each fragment, sample the `positionMap` to retrieve the world-space position $(pos.x, pos.y, pos.z)$.
**Index Conversion:** Convert the sampled world position to voxel indices $(x, y, z)$ using the volume bounds and resolution.
**Voxel Update:** Write the result to the voxel storage.
If performing solid voxelization, fill the interior.
If performing surface voxelization, mark only the surface voxels.
*   **Boundary Conditions:** Positions outside the volume bounds result in negative or out-of-bounds indices.
